posts.text:
In May of last year, members of our North St. Louis community saw their homes leveled and neighborhoods devastated.

Many of them are still unhoused, living in tents, and waiting for relief.

I'm running to go back to Congress now to deliver for our neighbors who have been neglected by Ill-prepared representation.
posts.summary: Demands relief for unhoused community members after disaster

The AI data centers coming to our communities are driving up the cost of utilities and have the potential to cause adverse health effects.

Unsurprisingly, our current Congressman remains silent about it.

When I’m back in Congress, I’ll fight to stop data centers from coming to St. Louis, so that we don't repeat history and let our families and children suffer the consequences.

posts.text:
I’m heartbroken after the shooting that took the lives of two MetroBus passengers in Breckenridge Hills yesterday afternoon.

Our communities deserve true safety. That means greater investment in gun violence prevention, substance abuse treatment programs, and mental health services.

My prayers are with the victims' families and all who are grieving after this tragedy.
posts.summary: Calls for gun violence prevention and mental health investment

posts.text:
Today, we remember the 8372 lives lost in the Srebrenica genocide.

At the Sebilj of St. Louis, we mourned those murdered 31 years ago, keeping their memory alive to ensure that history can never repeat itself or be rewritten.

But the genocide is not ancient history. Srebrenica is in the living memory of countless families both in Bosnia and here in St. Louis who lost their brothers, sons, and fathers.

I’m proud to stand with St. Louis’ Bosnian community to commemorate thousands of Bosnian men
posts.summary: Commemorates Srebrenica genocide, warns against historical revisionism

posts.text:
I am saddened and angered by the bomb threat directed at Dar-ul-Islam, the largest mosque in our area, yesterday morning.

Islamophobia has become all too common in our current political environment. This kind of anti-Muslim bigotry has no place in St. Louis, or anywhere else. I'm thankful that nobody was harmed by this act of hate, and I am praying for everyone in our St. Louis Muslim community whose safety was threatened.
posts.summary: Condemns Islamophobia and bomb threats against mosque

posts.text:
The housing crisis is not new: it comes from decades of failed policies.

As someone who’s been unhoused, I know what it’s like to face the results of those policies.

When I saw that we had the power to stop a crisis, I knew we had the responsibility to take action.
posts.summary: Advocates action on housing crisis rooted in failed policies

On August 4th, our movement will go back to the House, and we’ll work to enshrine the right to an abortion in the Constitution.
